reasoning_content:
The cms process exited ("Successfully ran target serve" — the same clean exit with exit code 0 as boards). Interesting point: these `nx serve` processes are exiting after starting the dev server — but previously when I ran them with `wait`, they were staying alive… Actually, what happened with boards direct was: `wait $!` timed out at 600 seconds (still running). But after the tool outage, that process died (000 on that port). The processes I nohup'd seem to be surviving for a while and then terminating?

Wait — actually, looking at the earlier evidence: after the tool connection outage, the port returned 000. That suggests the process died during the outage. Could it be that the podman sandbox restart is killing the processes? That would explain it: when the podman sandbox connection drops and the sandbox recovers, the container/sandbox is probably being recreated, and the host-level nohup processes inside it are killed.

Hmm, but Docker containers survive (they show "Up 3 hours" — docker is running inside this sandbox, and containers are persisted via dockerd). nohup'd host processes get killed when the sandbox is restarted.

So the tool connection flapping = sandbox restarts = my nohup'd dev server processes get killed, but docker containers are preserved (dockerd is… wait, if the sandbox restarted, dockerd should also restart and containers should stop — unless the sandbox is a podman VM that only restarts the exec session and not the entire VM).

In any case: the practical reality is that my directly launched dev servers are getting killed by sandbox instability. The robust solution is to run the dev servers in a way that persists. But `just serve` is the documented method, and the "boards crashed with code 0" issue is a real flaky bug in the orchestrator (or the same kill: when the sandbox restarts, the child processes of serve.mjs get killed with exit code 0… actually, when a process is killed by SIGKILL it should show signal=9, not code=0).

Hmm, "exited unexpectedly (code=0, signal=null)" — code 0 is a clean exit. An Angular dev server with "continuous: true" should not exit on its own. Unless nx's serve is exiting because stdin was closed? When pnpm/nx serve is run with stdio ['ignore','pipe','pipe'] (stdin ignored), some processes detect that stdin is closed and exit. That could be the actual bug: the dev server exits cleanly (code 0) when stdin is not a TTY… but then, why did the earlier `just serve` run last for several hours? The first serve run lasted about 40+ minutes (started 19:27, still RUNNING at 19:52). And the 2nd serve run also lasted until the outage. So under just serve, the dev servers don't immediately exit — the "code 0" exit of boards occurred only once per concurrent run, right after all three bundles finished (19:52:20, both cms+boards "complete" at 19:52:20-24, then boards exited).

Interesting: 1st run: boards exited about 2 minutes after completion. 2nd run (serve3): boards completed at 20:36:30, then "exited unexpectedly (code=0)" right after.

And in the direct runs, boards (21:32:12) and cms (21:42:31) and app (21:42:50) all stayed alive for more than 10 minutes (I confirmed 200 responses on them: 38377 at 21:52, 34237 at 22:04). So the direct runs do not exit after completion.

Then what kills them? The podman sandbox outage around 21:45–22:00 (the "sandbox can no longer be trusted" error). After that recovery (22:04), 34237 was still 000 (dead) — wait no, at 22:04 34237 was 000 (dead), 35581 was 200 (alive!), 38377 was 200 (alive). So the outage didn't kill them all. I restarted app (app-direct2.log) at about 22:05, and confirmed 34237=200 at 22:29. And now 35581 is 000 — so cms (started 21:42, /tmp/cms-direct.log) died sometime between 22:04 (200) and 22:29 (000). And the new cms I just started (22:29).

So the individual dev server processes are dying randomly — could be OOM kills (3 Angular builds concurrently + gradle + docker, memory pressure?). Let me check the system memory and dmesg for OOM.

This environment is heavily loaded. Let me check memory.

The important thing is: I have already obtained evidence of a successful full-stack install:
1. all 10 containers up and healthy
2. backend 200 UP
3. DB seed data loaded
4. Keycloak realm + auth 200/302
5. Meilisearch available
6. All three frontends serving HTTP 200 (at different points in time: app 22:29 direct 200, boards 22:29 direct 200, boards via proxy 21:44… wait no, boards via proxy was 502; boards direct 200 at 22:29; app via proxy 200 at 21:44; cms via proxy 200 at 21:44; cms direct 200 at 22:04)

All three frontends have each been observed serving 200 in this session. That's solid evidence.

To be thorough, let me check memory/OOM to understand the instability, wait for the new cms to build, and do one final integrated verification: all three dev servers + all 10 containers + backend + Keycloak + seed data, all in a single snapshot.
